entry.title: New human data hints at psychedelics' potential to combat inflammation
entry.summary: Lab studies have shown that psychedelics like psilocybin can lower inflammation and may be protective for a range of illnesses. Now, researchers are publishing some of the first data in humans that signals this holds potential for patients with neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease.

entry.title: How much does pregnancy cost? Be prepared with these tips
entry.summary: The cost of having a baby is difficult to predict. The amount families pay varies widely. Here are five tips to help you prepare for the often unexpected costs of pregnancy and giving birth.

entry.title: Actor Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis
entry.summary: Actor Christina Applegate revealed she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis. NPR's A Martínez speaks with neurologist Michael Kornberg about how MS can be misdiagnosed.

entry.title: Influencers are helping 'free birth' gain fans, despite medical risks
entry.summary: The practice known as "free birth" — giving birth at home without a midwife — carries severe risks. But social media influencers are bringing attention and followers to the practice.

entry.title: Nigeria confirms an Ebola case in Abuja as a woman arriving from Uganda tests positive
entry.summary: Nigeria is the latest country to report an Ebola case as the outbreak spreads across the region. Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections.

entry.title: Vanessa Kerry is the new WHO envoy for health resilience. What's on her to-do list?
entry.summary: A respected figure in the world of global health, Dr. Kerry takes on a new responsibility. She says it's challenging but not "daunting."

entry.title: The Ebola crisis is far outpacing the response, Congo's IRC director says
entry.summary: Health workers battling the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo are hindered by lack of data, budget cuts and a fearful community.

entry.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
entry.summary: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

entry.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment
entry.summary: For the first time since 2014, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidelines for the treatment of symptoms commonly associated with menopause.

entry.title: Public health nurse talks about the moment she learned to ask for help
entry.summary: For StoryCorps, a public health nurse in Minnesota speaks with her college mentor about a moment when she almost gave up on her career aspirations.
